report: Facilitation complete for this session. All three sisters' concerns were heard directly and recorded as confirmed noncontroversial essences: C wants a genuinely fair share with no subsidizing of a discount and time to consider; A wants an affordable, sustainable purchase freely agreed by all three; B wants funds toward a dance studio and to understand options before deciding; and all three (plus me, as participant) confirmed that any agreement must be free of pressure, with no penalty for saying no. Three draft options were circulated and neither accepted nor rejected: (1) independent valuation with transparent price, (2) any family discount absorbed by A's own inheritance share, (3) open-market sale. Key unresolved items: how price and split would be decided under option 1; whether A's share could cover a discount and keep the purchase affordable under option 2; what happens if an open-market sale yields too little for B's studio needs. Nothing is agreed — everyone explicitly reserved the right to say no, and C confirmed no deadline pressure. Next step would be working through the open questions, likely starting with an independent valuation to give everyone shared facts. I made no legal decisions or financial moves.
